title: Transport statistics and thermoelectric performance of Hofstadters butterfly
abstract: We investigate electrons subject to a magnetic field that may tunnel along a square lattice and additionally to two electronic leads. Using non-equilibrium Greens functions we evaluate the transmission and from that particle and energy currents and zero-frequency noise of the setup. We identify sweet spots for which the transmission reaches unity over broad frequency windows -- carried by topologically protected boundary modes that are quite robust against local fluctuations of on-site energies. These transmission plateaus can be exploited for the implementation robust current standards, clocks and thermoelectric devices.
summary: This work analyzes electron transport in the Hofstadter model under a magnetic field, using non-equilibrium Green's functions. It reveals that topologically protected boundary modes create regions of near-perfect transmission, which can be utilized for building highly reliable quantum standards and energy devices. The theoretical framework also rigorously connects transport properties to fundamental thermodynamic laws.
main_problem: The paper investigates the transport statistics and thermoelectric performance of electrons in a lattice subjected to a magnetic field, focusing on identifying robust transport features.
main_result: The study identifies 'sweet spots' characterized by near-unit transmission plateaus, which are carried by topologically protected boundary modes robust against local disorder. These features are promising for developing robust quantum devices.
method: The analysis employs non-equilibrium Green's functions to calculate transport quantities like particle and energy currents, as well as zero-frequency noise and entropy production rate.
model_or_system: The system is modeled by electrons tunneling on a square lattice under a perpendicular magnetic field, described by the Hofstadter Hamiltonian. The system is coupled to semi-infinite leads acting as reservoirs.
key_observables: Transmission function T(w), Matter current (I_M), Energy current (I_E), Zero-frequency noise (S_M), and Entropy production rate (sigma).
important_parameters: Magnetic flux per plaquette (B), coupling strength (tau), and bias/temperature gradients.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes non-interacting electrons and relies on the framework of non-equilibrium Green's functions for transport calculations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the Hofstadter butterfly structure (level density vs. B), the evolution of transmission T(w) with coupling strength, and plots contrasting boundary mode transport versus bulk mode transport.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the theoretical framework using non-equilibrium Green's functions to calculate transport observables. It then analyzes the model's behavior across different magnetic field regimes and coupling strengths, culminating in the identification of topologically protected transport channels and deriving thermodynamic bounds.
why_interesting: The connection between topological protection, robust transport (near-unity transmission), and thermodynamic quantities like entropy production makes this highly relevant for understanding energy flow and dissipation in quantum mesoscopic systems.
